newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian share index ends little changed.
newsitem.headline: Russian share index ends little changed.

text.p: Leading Russian shares closed mixed on Thursday in lethargic, low volume trading due to the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares rose by 0.69 percent to 188.42 on volume of $9.78 million.
"The market has jumped down a bit," said Oleg Mamontov, a trader at Alfa-Rinaco.

He said the market ignored news that the UES utility monopoly planned to protest against a decision by the State Anti-Monopoly Committee allowing independent utility Irkutskenergo to export electricity to Mongolia.
"People think Irkutskenergo will win and the buying is prompted by Irkutskenergo plans to issue American Depositary Receipts," he said.
Irkutskenergo was $0.123 after $0.1235, UES ordinary fell to $0.0813 from $0.0818, UES preferred were $0.0624 after $0.0627.
Traders said the market was positive about government plans to sell shares in telecommunications holding AO Svyazinvest and they predicted a rise in Rostelekom shares on Friday.
"Rostelekom has already discounted the news a bit," said Dmitry Yevenko, chief trader at United City Bank.
As part of the strategy to sell Svyazinvest, the government plans to transfer its 38 percent stake, equal to 51 percent of voting shares, in Rostelekom to Svyazinvest.
Mamontov said the market would wait for the State Duma lower house non-binding decision on whether to impeach President Boris Yeltsin.
Yeltsin's communist opponents Duma said on Monday they would try and impeach him. The Duma will discuss the issue tomorrow.
"I think now is the time to buy, after the fall of the last few days," Mamontov said. "If the Duma fails to impeach the president, prices will rise."

Yuganskneftegaz fell to $6.35 from $9.60 at Wednesday's close, Mosenergo was $0.979 after $0.975, Norilsk Nickel edged down to $5.80 from $5.90 and Murmanskelectro rose to $10.50 from $7.20 at the November 4 close, when it was last traded.
